descripcion_es: Literature, cinema, music, visual arts and heritage.
resumen: Vocabulary for talking about and giving opinions on books, films, exhibitions and cultural heritage in an educated register, as in a review or an informed conversation.

explicacion.texto: Besides the nouns, evaluative adjectives and the collocations used by critics matter: a novel is “set in” a place, a film “stars” an actor, a play is “staged”, an exhibition “features” works.

filas: long work of fiction / short work of fiction / short non-fiction piece giving the author's views (es: novela / relato / ensayo)
Her first novel became a bestseller.
the series of events in a story (es: argumento, trama)
The plot is hard to follow.
a person in a story / the most important person in it (es: personaje / protagonista)
The main character is a retired teacher.
to take place in a particular place or time (es: estar ambientada en)
The story is set in 1930s Madrid.
to have as the main actor / with as the main actor (es: protagonizar / protagonizada por)
all the actors in a film or play (es: reparto)
person who directs a film / written text of a film (es: director / guion)
It won the award for best screenplay.
to present a play / an act of performing (es: poner en escena / representación, actuación)
The play was first staged in 1605.
public display of art / to show it publicly (es: exposición / exponer)
The exhibition features works by Goya.
a work of outstanding quality (es: obra maestra)
history and culture passed down / a place protected by UNESCO (es: patrimonio / Patrimonio de la Humanidad)
The old town is a World Heritage Site.
to repair something old to its original state / the process (es: restaurar / restauración)
three-dimensional work / picture made with paint / picture of a person (es: escultura / cuadro / retrato)
painting of the countryside / painting of objects such as fruit or flowers (es: paisaje / bodegón)
of the present time / new and experimental (es: contemporáneo / vanguardista)
written opinion of a work / person who writes it / detailed critical analysis (es: reseña, crítica / crítico / análisis crítico)
highly praised / highly praised by critics (es: aclamado / aclamado por la crítica)
making people think seriously (es: que invita a la reflexión)
so exciting you cannot stop (es: apasionante / absorbente)
valued more / less than it deserves (es: sobrevalorado / infravalorado)
I think the series is overrated.
ticket office; commercial success / big, expensive, very popular film (es: taquilla / superproducción, éxito de taquilla)
to be made available to the public for the first time / the act of doing so (es: estrenarse / estreno)
The film was released in May.

items: “Critic” is the person; “review” is the piece they write; “criticism” is criticism in the negative sense.
“Argument” is not the plot of a film (Spanish “argumento”): that is “plot”.
“Character” = a person in the story; “actor / actress” = the person who plays them.

ejemplos.frase: The novel is set in a fishing village on the Galician coast.
ejemplos.traduccion: La novela está ambientada en un pueblo pesquero de la costa gallega.

ejemplos.frase: The exhibition features more than a hundred works by Sorolla.
ejemplos.traduccion: La exposición reúne más de cien obras de Sorolla.

ejemplos.frase: Her latest film received rave reviews at Cannes.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su última película recibió críticas entusiastas en Cannes.

ejemplos.frase: The Alhambra is one of Spain's best-known World Heritage Sites.
ejemplos.traduccion: La Alhambra es uno de los lugares Patrimonio de la Humanidad más conocidos de España.

ejemplos.frase: I found the ending rather disappointing, but the plot is gripping.
ejemplos.traduccion: El final me pareció algo decepcionante, pero la trama engancha.

ejemplos.frase: The play has been staged all over the world.
ejemplos.traduccion: La obra se ha representado en todo el mundo.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The argument of the film is very original.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The plot of the film is very original.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The plot of a work (Spanish “argumento”) is “plot”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The critic of the book was very negative.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The review of the book was very negative.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The written review is “review”; “critic” is the person.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The film was estrenated last week.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The film was released last week.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: To “estrenar” a film is “release”; a play “premieres” or “opens”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The novel is situated in Paris.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The novel is set in Paris.

ejercicios.frase: The novel is ___ in Barcelona during the Civil War.
ejercicios.explicacion: The collocation on the card is to be set in = to take place in, the fixed form for saying where and when a story happens. The clue is that we are talking about a novel and a place and period. Set is the past participle of set (set, set, set), so is set in Barcelona is the only natural combination.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Be set in” = to take place in (es: estar ambientada en).
ejercicios.traduccion: La novela está ambientada en Barcelona durante la Guerra Civil.

por_opcion.set: Correct: be set in is the fixed collocation for the setting of a work of fiction.
por_opcion.placed: Incorrect: place means to put something somewhere physically; it is not used for the setting of a story.
por_opcion.situated: Incorrect: situated describes the real location of a building or place (The hotel is situated near the beach), not the setting of a novel.
por_opcion.located at: Incorrect: located describes where something physically is and, besides, at does not fit with a city; for fiction we say set in.

ejercicios.frase: I didn't understand the argument of the film at all.
respuestas: I didn't understand the plot of the film at all.
I didn't understand the storyline of the film at all.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that argument is not the plot of a film: in English an argument is a quarrel or a line of reasoning to defend a position. The plot (Spanish “argumento” or “trama”) is plot, and storyline is a slightly more informal synonym. So you must replace argument with plot (or storyline) and leave the rest unchanged.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The plot of a film is “plot”.
ejercicios.traduccion: No entendí nada el argumento de la película.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I didn't understand the argument of the film at all.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: argument is a false friend and means a quarrel or a line of reasoning.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I didn't understand the history of the film at all.
errores_previstos.explicacion: History is history as a subject or the past; the plot of a film is plot or storyline.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I didn't understand the theme of the film at all.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Theme is the underlying subject (love, war), not the sequence of events that make up the plot.

glosario.definicion_l: a secret scheme to do something (especially something underhand or illegal) · a small area of ground covered by specific vegetation
the plot of a book or play or film
a fact or assertion offered as evidence that something is true · a contentious speech act; a dispute where there is strong disagreement

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (es: obra maestra).
ejercicios.frase: Many consider Don Quixote the first modern novel and a ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The word on the card is masterpiece: a work of exceptional quality in an art form. It is a countable noun, so it takes a (a masterpiece). The clue is the highest praise given to Don Quixote in the sentence.
ejercicios.traduccion: Muchos consideran el Quijote la primera novela moderna y una obra maestra.

errores_previstos.respuesta: master piece
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is written as one word: masterpiece.

errores_previstos.respuesta: masterpieces
errores_previstos.explicacion: After a, the noun is singular: a masterpiece.

glosario.definicion_l: the most outstanding work of a creative artist or craftsman · an outstanding achievement

ejercicios.frase: The film ___ two of Spain's best-known actors.
ejercicios.explicacion: According to the table, to star is a transitive verb whose subject is the film: The film stars X = X plays the main role in the film. The clue is that the subject is The film and the actors follow as the direct object. That is why stars, with no preposition.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Star” as a verb = to have as the main actor.
ejercicios.traduccion: La película está protagonizada por dos de los actores españoles más conocidos.

por_opcion.stars: Correct: the film stars + actor is the usual collocation (Spanish “protagonizar”).
por_opcion.protagonises: Incorrect: it is a calque of Spanish; the verb is not used in English with this meaning.
por_opcion.acts: Incorrect: act is what the actor does (He acts in the film), not the film; besides, it is intransitive here.
por_opcion.features in: Incorrect: feature in has the actor as its subject (Two actors feature in the film); with the film as the subject you would say features, without in.

glosario.significado: estar protagonizada por (con la película como sujeto)

glosario.definicion_l: most familiar or renowned

ejercicios.frase: Segovia's aqueduct is part of our cultural ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes heritage, the historical and cultural legacy of a country. The collocation cultural heritage is fixed, and heritage is uncountable, so it takes neither a nor a plural. The clue is part of our cultural…, which calls for the whole body of inherited assets.
ejercicios.traduccion: El acueducto de Segovia forma parte de nuestro patrimonio cultural.

errores_previstos.respuesta: inheritance
errores_previstos.explicacion: Inheritance is what a person receives when someone dies (property, money); a country's cultural legacy is cultural heritage.

errores_previstos.respuesta: heritages
errores_previstos.explicacion: Heritage is uncountable in this use and has no plural.

glosario.definicion_l: practices that are handed down from the past by tradition · any attribute or immaterial possession that is inherited from ancestors
a conduit that resembles a bridge but carries water over a valley

ejercicios.frase: The critic of the exhibition in El País was very positive.
respuestas: The review of the exhibition in El País was very positive.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list on the card separates critic (the person who writes the review) from review (the written assessment). The clue is that what was positive is a text about an exhibition published in a newspaper, that is, a review: The review.
ejercicios.traduccion: La crítica de la exposición en El País fue muy positiva.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The critic of the exhibition in El País was very positive.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: critic is the person who writes reviews.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The criticism of the exhibition in El País was very positive.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Criticism suggests disapproval, negative criticism; a positive assessment is a review.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The critique of the exhibition in El País was very positive.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Critique is a detailed critical analysis, in an academic register; a press review is review.

glosario.definicion_l: a new appraisal or evaluation · an essay or article that gives a critical evaluation (as of a book or play)
a person who is professionally engaged in the analysis and interpretation of works of art · anyone who expresses a reasoned judgment of something
the act of exhibiting · a collection of things (goods or works of art etc.) for public display

ejercicios.frase: The new Almodóvar film will be ___ in cinemas next month.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table shows that showing a film in cinemas for the first time is to be released. The clue is in cinemas: we are talking about making it available to the public in commercial cinemas. Premiere is used for a gala first night or for a play, and open rather for plays or exhibitions.
ejercicios.traduccion: La nueva película de Almodóvar se estrenará en los cines el mes que viene.

por_opcion.released: Correct: be released in cinemas = to come out in cinemas (es: estrenarse en salas).
por_opcion.premiered on: Incorrect: premiere refers to a specific first showing (premiered at Cannes) and on does not fit with in cinemas.
por_opcion.launched off: Incorrect: launch is used for products or campaigns, and launch off does not exist with this meaning.
por_opcion.opened: Incorrect here: open is used with plays or exhibitions (The play opens on Friday), and in the passive it does not work with a film.

ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card, cast is all the actors in a work. The expression all-star cast means a cast full of stars. The clue is all-star, which only combines with a noun that refers to the performers as a group.
ejercicios.traduccion: La película tiene un reparto de estrellas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: casting
errores_previstos.explicacion: Casting is the process of choosing actors, not the result; the group of actors is cast.

errores_previstos.respuesta: distribution
errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of Spanish “reparto”: distribution is the commercial distribution of the film.

glosario.definicion_l: the actors in a play · container into which liquid is poured to create a given shape when it hardens

ejercicios.frase: It's a ___ thriller: I couldn't put it down.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes gripping = so exciting you cannot stop. It is an -ing adjective because it describes the effect the work has on the reader. The clue is I couldn't put it down, a typical sign of an absorbing book.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es un thriller apasionante: no podía dejar de leerlo.

por_opcion.gripping: Correct: an -ing adjective describing a work that holds the reader's attention.
por_opcion.gripped: Incorrect: the -ed adjective describes the person (I was gripped), not the work.
por_opcion.griping: Incorrect: with a single p it comes from gripe (to complain) and means “complaining”.
por_opcion.grasping: Incorrect: grasping means greedy or holding tightly; it does not apply to a book.

glosario.definicion_l: capable of arousing and holding the attention

ejercicios.frase: In my opinion, that band is completely ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives overrated = valued more than its real quality deserves. Its opposite is underrated. The clue is In my opinion together with completely, which introduces a critical, negative assessment of the band's fame.
ejercicios.traduccion: En mi opinión, ese grupo está completamente sobrevalorado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: overvalued
errores_previstos.explicacion: Overvalued is used mainly in economics (a currency, a share); for works or artists we say overrated.

errores_previstos.respuesta: underrated
errores_previstos.explicacion: Underrated is the opposite: valued less than it deserves.

glosario.definicion_l: make too high an estimate of
an unofficial association of people or groups · instrumentalists not including string players

ejercicios.frase: Velázquez painted several ___ of the royal family.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table on the card includes portrait = a picture of a person. The clue is painted and of the royal family: these are paintings that represent specific people. Portraits is the regular plural and the of is already in the sentence.
ejercicios.traduccion: Velázquez pintó varios retratos de la familia real.

por_opcion.pictures of: Incorrect: it would repeat of (pictures of of the royal family) and picture is too general.
por_opcion.retreats: Incorrect: a false friend because of its similar form; a retreat is a quiet place to rest or a withdrawal.
por_opcion.portrays: Incorrect: portray is a verb (to depict, to represent), not a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: a word picture of a person's appearance and character · any likeness of a person, in any medium
royal persons collectively

ejercicios.frase: The film was a huge box-___ success.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes box office = ticket office, and as an adjective box-office success or box-office hit = commercial success. The clue is the first part of the compound, box-, and the commercial sense of huge success.
ejercicios.traduccion: La película fue un enorme éxito de taquilla.

errores_previstos.respuesta: ticket
errores_previstos.explicacion: Box-ticket does not exist; the ticket office is the box office.

errores_previstos.respuesta: offices
errores_previstos.explicacion: In the adjectival compound the noun is singular: box-office success.

glosario.definicion_l: total admission receipts for an entertainment · the office where tickets of admission are sold
unusually great in size or amount or degree or especially extent or scope

ejercicios.frase: Her essay is ___: it made me rethink many of my ideas.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives thought-provoking = making people think seriously, literally provoking thoughts. The clue is the second part: it made me rethink many of my ideas. It is an evaluative compound adjective widely used in cultural criticism.
ejercicios.traduccion: Su ensayo invita a la reflexión: me hizo replantearme muchas de mis ideas.

por_opcion.thought-provoking: Correct: it describes a work that makes you think.
por_opcion.thoughtless: Incorrect: it means inconsiderate or careless, a negative sense.
por_opcion.thought-out: Incorrect: it is used as well thought-out (carefully planned); it does not describe the effect on the reader.
por_opcion.overthought: Incorrect: it means thought about too much, over-elaborate.

glosario.definicion_l: stimulating interest or thought
an analytic or interpretive literary composition · a tentative attempt

ejercicios.frase: The story is situated in a small town in Castile.
respuestas: The story is set in a small town in Castile.
ejercicios.explicacion: As on the card (The novel is situated in Paris), situated describes the real location of something, not the setting of a work of fiction. For the setting, use be set in. The clue is The story: we are talking about a narrative.
ejercicios.traduccion: La historia está ambientada en un pueblo pequeño de Castilla.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The story is situated in a small town in Castile.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: situated does not work for the setting of a story.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The story is located in a small town in Castile.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Located, like situated, indicates physical location; for fiction we say set in.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The story is placed in a small town in Castile.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Placed means put somewhere; the correct collocation is be set in.

glosario.definicion_l: a region of central Spain; a former kingdom that comprised most of modern Spain and united with Aragon to form Spain in 1479

respuestas: The cathedral is currently being restored
The cathedral is being restored currently
Currently the cathedral is being restored
ejercicios.explicacion: The sentence uses the continuous passive: is being + past participle (restored), for an action in progress whose subject, the cathedral, receives the action. The table on the card includes to restore / restoration. Currently, an adverb of time, fits naturally between the auxiliary and being, or at the beginning of the sentence (Currently, the cathedral is being restored); at the end it is also accepted, although it sounds less natural.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Continuous passive: is being + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: La catedral está siendo restaurada en este momento.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The cathedral is currently restored being
errores_previstos.explicacion: Being goes before the past participle: is being restored.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Currently the cathedral being is restored
errores_previstos.explicacion: The order of the continuous passive is is + being + past participle.

glosario.definicion_l: at this time or period; now
relating to or containing or issuing from a bishop's office or throne · any large and important church

descripcion_larga_es: Vocabulary for talking fluently about books, cinema, theatre, the visual arts and heritage: not only the nouns (plot, cast, masterpiece, heritage) but also the collocations critics use (a novel is set in, a film stars, an exhibition features). It matters because it is common in educated conversation and in the press, and because it contains very treacherous false friends for a Spanish speaker, such as argument, critic or situated.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of cultural criticism and heritage: types of work, elements of a narrative (plot, character, setting), professionals (director, cast, critic), assessments (gripping, overrated, thought-provoking) and concepts of heritage and restoration.
contexto.por_que_importa: In a C1-level conversation you are expected to recommend or criticise a work precisely, not just say it is good or bad. The false friends in this field (argument, critic, situated, Spanish “estrenar”) produce sentences that a native speaker understands but that reveal the calque, and in an oral exam they make you sound less natural.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When discussing a film or a book, reviewing an exhibition, talking about a city's heritage or reading the culture section of a newspaper. The signals are critics' verbs (set, star, stage, feature, release) and evaluative adjectives. Spanish speakers tend to translate word for word: “argumento” as argument, or “estrenar” with an invented verb.
